title: Micro-hub swimlane: compact workspace tiles and lane-based navigation
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and prototype a compact ‘micro-hub’ swimlane UI for the Redwood Console sidebar that presents workspace-level tiles (quick state, recent routes, pinned dashboards) in a horizontally scrollable lane. Goal is to reduce context-switch time, make dashboard routing discoverable, and provide lightweight controls for rollouts/canaries without leaving the current view. This pattern should support quick workspace switching, preserve persistent long-lived dashboards, and surface per-route cost/latency badges. Deliverables: high-fidelity Figma frames, interactive prototype, annotated handoff specs, and a short usability test report.
acceptance_criteria: Tile lane shows up to 8 workspace tiles and supports keyboard navigation and horizontal scroll on small widths
Each tile displays workspace name, last-active route, cost badge, and a three-dot context menu for rollouts and settings
Clicking a tile routes to the workspace landing; pressing space when a tile is focused opens quick actions without full route change
Design tokens and spacing follow console theme; responsive collapse to single-icon compact rail at <900px
Prototype validated with at least 6 usability sessions; median task completion time reduced by 18% vs baseline
engineering_notes: Prefer CSS transform-based horizontal scroll with 'will-change: transform' for smoothness
Add aria roles for listbox and menu; keyboard shortcuts to jump to next/previous tile (Ctrl+J / Ctrl+K)
Cost and latency badges should be rendered server-side to avoid jank; provide lightweight cache headers
Tile prefetch: fetch small route metadata on hover/focus (200ms debounce) to warmup landing data

risks_and_tradeoffs: Adding an always-visible lane increases cognitive density in sidebar; mitigated via progressive disclosure (collapse to icons) and a user preference to pin/unpin
Prefetching route metadata improves perceived speed but increases API load — limited with debounce and user-driven fetch triggers
Rendering live cost badges could leak small telemetry spikes; proposed server-side aggregation and a one-minute refresh cadence
